one_liner: Rust port of d3-geo-voronoi (spherical Delaunay/Voronoi); its wasm canvas demo draws frames about 1.95x faster than the JS original.
what_it_does: Computes the Delaunay triangulation of points given in longitude/latitude on the sphere and its dual Voronoi diagram, following d3-geo-voronoi's design. You build a Voronoi<T> with Voronoi::try_from(Geometry::MultiPoint(...)) and then ask for polygons(), triangles(), mesh(), links(), hull(), cell_mesh() or find(), getting geo-types/d3_geo_rs FeatureCollections back; the method names mirror the JS API, but it is a Rust crate (d3_geo_voronoi_rs) and is meant to be drawn with the author's d3_geo_rs port of d3-geo.
how_it_is_fast: It uses the same algorithm as the JavaScript library: points are projected, triangulated with a planar Delaunay (d3_delaunay_rs over delaunator), and circumcenters, cell polygons, neighbours, mesh, hull and the Urquhart graph are all computed once at construction. The speed difference is plain compilation to wasm with f64 math and no garbage collector (the README's own explanation), not a new algorithm; the benchmarked frame is mostly d3_geo_rs orthographic projection, clipping and resampling plus canvas drawing.
when_to_use: Rust or Rust-to-wasm code that needs spherical Voronoi cells or Delaunay meshes for a few hundred to a few thousand points, e.g. drawing them on a rotating globe on a canvas.
Porting a d3-geo-voronoi visualisation to Rust while keeping its method names (polygons, triangles, mesh, links, hull, find).
Native Rust tools that render spherical Voronoi diagrams to SVG through d3_geo_rs (the profile_target binary and the criterion bench draw 600 and 6000 cells this way).
Animated browser globes where the JS page misses a 16 ms frame budget: the author's page fit 1220 points per frame against 600 for JS.
when_not_to_use: JavaScript projects that just want a faster npm drop-in: the README documents no npm or wasm package, so you must write your own wasm-bindgen wrapper the way benchmark/src/lib.rs does.
f32 workloads: the README says cells break (some take up the whole sphere) unless T is f64.
Hard inputs that need a robust hull: the README lists a failing test, 'geoVoronoi.hull does not break on difficult polygons'.
Contours: contour.js and its tests are not ported.
Multithreaded or web-worker sharing of one diagram: Delaunay holds Rc fields and a boxed non-Send closure, so the Voronoi value cannot cross threads.

integration.dependencies: d3_geo_rs 3.1.3, d3_delaunay_rs 0.11.3, geo 0.31, geo-types 0.7.17, delaunator 1, approx, num-traits, float_next_after; the workspace build patches geo/geo-types to the author's cyclic_match git branch and delaunator to its git master
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 2021 edition; no rust-version declared on crates.io (MSRV not documented); benchmark needs wasm-pack, webpack 5 and npm
integration.platforms: any Rust target; the demo targets wasm32-unknown-unknown with getrandom's wasm_js backend
integration.thread_safety: not documented; Voronoi/Delaunay contain Rc and a Box<dyn Fn> without Send, so they are single-threaded only
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — method names follow d3-geo-voronoi, but it is a Rust API (TryFrom<Geometry>, FeatureCollection from d3_geo_rs) with no published JS binding

gotchas: The benchmark does not time the Voronoi computation: both pages build the diagram once on slider change (update() in Rust, gen_points() in JS) and time only the per-frame render: polygons() rebuilt from cached Delaunay data, orthographic projection with rotation, path generation and canvas fill/stroke of every cell and point. The 1.95x therefore reflects mostly d3_geo_rs path/projection code plus identical canvas work, not this crate's triangulation.

The comparison is first-party on both sides: the JS benchmark page in Fil/d3-geo-voronoi (benchmark/sphereCanvas.html) was contributed by the same author (PRs #31, #43, #45) and loads an unpinned d3@7 from unpkg; no browser, CPU, run count or variance is given for the 8.165 ms figure, and the Rust timer also includes the clearRect call that the JS timer excludes (a small bias against Rust).

README build steps say cd benchmark\www, but package.json now sits directly in benchmark/; the JS page now lives at benchmark/sphereCanvas.html, not src/benchmark/. The JS page's slider stops at 1000 points while the Rust page goes to 6000.

The numbers date from 2023-08-20 (when issue #2 'Restore benchmark' was closed) and were not re-measured for 0.10.x; issue #1 (open since 2023-04-03) notes the demo re-sends the same colour strings to JS each frame instead of interning them.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No catalogued sibling covers spherical Voronoi or Delaunay, so pick it whenever you need that geometry in Rust or wasm; contour-wasm (1.3x to 2.0x over MarchingSquares.js isoBands) is the nearest geographic wasm entry and is the one to use for contour bands, which this port lacks.
verified_claims_summary: In the author's own browser test (browser and hardware unstated, 2023), the JS d3-geo-voronoi canvas page needed about 16 ms per frame to draw 600 random points' Voronoi cells on a rotating orthographic globe, while the Rust/wasm port drew the same scene in 8.165 ms (1.95x) and fitted 1220 points in 16 ms; only the per-frame projection and drawing are timed, not the diagram construction.
status_note: Lightly active single-author port (latest crates.io release 0.10.7 on 2025-07-24, about 43,000 downloads, 8 stars, no GitHub releases); MIT declared in Cargo.toml without a LICENSE file (the benchmark's package.json says MIT OR Apache-2.0), usable from Rust if you stay on f64.
